examBlueprint.speaking: Integrated 30 mins · 60m prep -> 5–10m concise critical synthesis of audio + 10m personal thesis + 10m razor-sharp jury debate.

modules.title: Mise en Relief, Formal Inversion & Stylistic Cadence
modules.summary: Shape sentence focus and rhythm like a published French essayist using cleft structures, adverbial inversion, and balanced periods.
objectives: Spotlight precise ideas with French clefting ("Ce qui frappe..., c’est...", "C’est précisément dans... que réside...").
Apply literary/formal inversion cleanly after aussi, ainsi, encore, peut-être, sans doute, à peine, en vain.
Balance long periodic sentences with punchy short conclusions for compelling oral and written cadence.
grammarCheckpoints: Syntactic mise en relief (c’est... qui/que, ce qui... c’est)
Adverbial inversion (Aussi convient-il, Encore faut-il, À peine avait-il)

drills.title: Cadence & Mise en Relief Transformation
drills.instruction: Rewrite 4 flat subject-verb-object statements using cleft emphasis and formal inversion ("Encore faut-il...", "Aussi...").

drills.title: Rhetorical Opening Speech Sprint
drills.instruction: Deliver a 90-second keynote opening on civic trust combining one cleft sentence, one inversion, and one sharp rhythmic pause.

modules.checkpointPrompt: Write a 125-word editorial opening on democratic trust using "C’est précisément...", "Encore faut-il...", "Aussi + inversion", and "résider dans".

lesson.overview: Move beyond error-free French into genuinely memorable French style — controlling where the listener’s ear lands on every single phrase.

sections.heading: Syntactic Mise en Relief (Spotlighting the Core Thesis)
sections.explanation: French relies less on vocal stress than English and more on syntax! Pull your focal concept into the spotlight with "C’est précisément [X] qui/que...", "Ce qui mérite d’être souligné, c’est...", or "S’il est un domaine où..., c’est bien...".
sections.formula: S’il est un [noun] qui..., c’est bien...  |  C’est précisément dans [X] que réside [Y]

examples.target: S’il est une illusion tenace, c’est bien de croire que la technique résout seule les conflits politiques.
examples.translation: If there is one stubborn illusion, it is indeed believing that technology alone solves political conflicts.
examples.highlight: S’il est une illusion ... c’est bien

examples.target: C’est précisément dans l’articulation entre liberté locale et solidarité nationale que réside l’équilibre.
examples.translation: It is precisely in the articulation between local freedom and national solidarity that the balance lies.

sections.proTip: In formal C2 style, notice the concise "S’il est un..." (dropping the "y a" of "S’il y a un...") — an instant mark of elegance!

sections.heading: Mandatory & Stylistic Formal Inversion
sections.explanation: Starting a clause with "encore" (still/yet), "aussi" (therefore), "à peine" (hardly), "du moins" (at least), or "peut-être" (perhaps) triggers graceful subject-verb inversion in C2 French: "Encore faut-il que...", "À peine la loi fut-elle votée que...", "Peut-être conviendrait-il...".
sections.formula: [Encore / Aussi / Peut-être / À peine / Sans doute] + Verb + Pronoun (+ noun subject before verb if present)

examples.target: L’ambition est louable ; encore faut-il que les moyens financiers suivent dans la durée.
examples.translation: The ambition is laudable; still, financial means must follow over the long term.

examples.target: Sans doute cette réforme appellera-t-elle des ajustements progressifs sur le terrain.
examples.translation: No doubt this reform will call for gradual adjustments in the field (complex noun + pronoun inversion!).

sections.proTip: When the subject is a full noun ("cette réforme"), use complex inversion: keep the noun before the verb AND echo it with a pronoun after the verb ("cette réforme appellera-t-elle")!

vocabCards.meaning: even so, it is still necessary to / that
vocabCards.example: Encore faut-il éviter que la norme n’étouffe l’initiative.
vocabCards.exampleNote: Followed by infinitive or "que + Subjonctif".

vocabCards.example: C’est précisément cette ambiguïté qu’il convient de lever.
vocabCards.exampleNote: Sharpens thesis focus instantly.

vocabCards.example: À peine l’accord était-il signé que de nouvelles tensions surgissaient.
vocabCards.exampleNote: Paired with "que" in the second clause.

vocabCards.example: En vain chercherait-on une solution unique à des crises si diverses.
vocabCards.exampleNote: Can trigger literary inversion in initial position.

vocabCards.example: La difficulté ne réside pas dans le diagnostic mais dans l’exécution.
vocabCards.exampleNote: Refined C2 verb replacing "être dans".

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which sentence demonstrates flawless complex noun-pronoun inversion after "Peut-être"?
options: Peut-être les citoyens attendent-ils davantage de clarté.
Peut-être attendent les citoyens davantage de clarté.
Peut-être les citoyens attendent davantage de clarté-ils.
practiceQuestions.explanation: In complex inversion, the noun stays before the verb and a matching subject pronoun is hyphenated after it: "les citoyens attendent-ils".

practiceQuestions.prompt: What nuance does "Encore faut-il que les collectivités disposent de ressources" add?
options: It repeats an earlier fact without adding conditions.
It introduces a crucial indispensable condition without which the preceding idea falls short.
It rejects the preceding idea completely.
practiceQuestions.explanation: "Encore faut-il que + Subjonctif" introduces a decisive necessary condition moderating an initial claim.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Listen to the keynote opener. Where does the speaker say the real remedy lies?
practiceQuestions.audioScript: S’il est une crise qui fragilise nos institutions, c’est bien l’érosion de la confiance civique. C’est précisément dans la transparence quotidienne de la décision publique que réside le premier remède.
options: In reducing the number of elections
In the daily transparency of public decision-making
practiceQuestions.explanation: The cleft structure spotlights "la transparence quotidienne de la décision publique" as the primary remedy.

lesson.checkpointModelAnswer: S’il est un capital immatériel dont la fragilité conditionne la vitalité de toute démocratie, c’est bien la confiance civique. En vain multiplierait-on les réformes techniques si les citoyens avaient le sentiment que les décisions majeures leur échappent durablement. C’est précisément dans la lisibilité des choix publics et la redevabilité réelle des responsables que réside la clé d’un renouveau institutionnel. L’essor des plateformes participatives témoigne certes d’une volonté d’écoute ; encore faut-il que les contributions citoyennes soient suivies d’effets concrets et motivés. Aussi convient-il d’inscrire durablement la délibération transparente au cœur de la gouvernance quotidienne, loin des effets d’annonce éphémères.

modules.title: Litote, Euphemism & Diplomatic Nuance (Ne serait pas sans...)
modules.summary: Persuade with razor-sharp French restraint using litotes, diplomatic Conditionnel, and concessive "quand bien même".
objectives: Deploy classic French litotes ("n’est pas sans poser problème", "ne saurait être ignoré", "il n’est pas exclu que").
Use "ne saurait + infinitive" (cannot possibly) and "quand bien même + Conditionnel" (even if) effortlessly.
Critique ideas rigorously in executive meetings or jury debates without ever sounding blunt or dogmatic.
grammarCheckpoints: Litotes (ne pas être sans + inf., ne pas laisser de)
Extreme concession: quand bien même + Conditionnel / avoir beau + Infinitive

drills.title: Diplomatic Critique Reframe Drill
drills.instruction: Soften 4 blunt criticisms ("C’est faux !", "Ça va échouer !") into razor-sharp diplomatic C2 litotes.

drills.title: Executive Policy Memo Paragraph
drills.instruction: Write 120 words warning a board about expansion risks using "ne serait pas sans", "ne saurait", and "quand bien même".

modules.checkpointPrompt: Write or deliver a 125-word diplomatic policy critique using "ne saurait", "n’est pas sans", "quand bien même", and "avoir beau".

lesson.overview: At C2, understatement carries far more authority than exclamation marks — master the classic French art of diplomatic precision.

sections.heading: French Litote & "Ne saurait" (Saying More by Saying Less)
sections.explanation: French intellectual discourse loves litote — expressing a strong judgment via double negation or deliberate restraint. "Cette décision n’est pas sans soulever des inquiétudes" hits harder in a boardroom or DALF C2 jury than "Tout le monde est furieux". Similarly, "ne saurait + inf." (without "pas"!) means "could not possibly / cannot legitimately".
sections.formula: X n’est pas sans + Infinitive  |  X ne saurait + Infinitive (no "pas"!)  |  Il n’est pas exclu que + Subj.

examples.target: Une dérégulation brutale ne serait pas sans fragiliser les acteurs les plus vulnérables.
examples.translation: Abrupt deregulation would not be without weakening (= would undeniably weaken) the most vulnerable actors.

examples.target: L’efficacité à court terme ne saurait justifier l’abandon des garanties fondamentales.
examples.translation: Short-term efficiency could never justify abandoning fundamental safeguards.

sections.proTip: Notice that "savoir" used as "ne saurait" (= cannot) drops "pas" completely! Never write "*ne saurait pas*".

sections.heading: Extreme Concession: Quand bien même & Avoir beau
sections.explanation: Concede the strongest possible version of an opponent’s premise before dismantling it: "Quand bien même + Conditionnel" ("Even if... were to...") and "Avoir beau + infinitive" ("No matter how much..."). Both give C2 persuasion devastating elegance.
sections.formula: Quand bien même + Conditionnel, [Conditionnel]  |  Subject + avoir beau + Infinitive, [Contrast]

examples.target: Quand bien même les algorithmes atteindraient une précision quasi parfaite, la responsabilité juridique demeurerait humaine.
examples.translation: Even if algorithms were to reach near-perfect accuracy, legal accountability would remain human.

examples.target: Les rapports ont beau s’accumuler depuis vingt ans, les arbitrages budgétaires tardent encore.
examples.translation: No matter how many reports pile up over twenty years, budgetary decisions are still delayed.

sections.proTip: "Avoir beau" is invariable — never agree "beau" in gender or number ("Elle a beau insister", "Ils ont beau essayer")!

vocabCards.example: Un tel compromis ne saurait satisfaire les exigences climatiques.
vocabCards.exampleNote: Never takes "pas"!

vocabCards.example: Quand bien même le financement serait acquis, le délai resterait irréaliste.
vocabCards.exampleNote: Takes Conditionnel.

vocabCards.meaning: to undeniably involve / not be without (litote)
vocabCards.example: Cette réorganisation n’est pas sans comporter certains risques.
vocabCards.exampleNote: Signature diplomatic understatement.

vocabCards.meaning: to do something in vain / no matter how much
vocabCards.example: On a beau multiplier les consignes, l’exemple compte davantage.
vocabCards.exampleNote: "Beau" never changes form.

vocabCards.meaning: it cannot be ruled out that (+ Subj.)
vocabCards.example: Il n’est pas exclu que cette tendance s’accélère dès l’an prochain.
vocabCards.exampleNote: Cautious C2 forecasting hedge.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Spot the single sentence with flawless C2 grammar:
options: Cette mesure ne saurait pas suffire et elles ont belles insister.
Cette mesure ne saurait suffire, et elles ont beau insister, le budget reste insuffisant.
Quand bien même le plan réussit, il ne saurait pas durer.
practiceQuestions.explanation: "Ne saurait" omits "pas", and "avoir beau" is always invariable ("elles ont beau insister").

practiceQuestions.prompt: What does a diplomat truly mean by "Ce calendrier n’est pas sans susciter de vives réserves"?
options: Everyone warmly approves of the schedule.
The schedule definitely triggers serious reservations (expressed via litote).
Nobody has read the schedule yet.
practiceQuestions.explanation: The double-negative litote "n’est pas sans + inf." emphatically affirms the existence of strong reservations while preserving diplomatic restraint.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Listen to the legal scholar. Does she think near-perfect AI accuracy removes human accountability?
practiceQuestions.audioScript: Quand bien même un système prédictif atteindrait une fiabilité de nonante-neuf pour cent, une telle performance ne saurait dispenser le décideur public d’assumer sa responsabilité devant le citoyen.
options: Yes, above 99% accuracy human accountability is no longer needed
No — even at 99% reliability, public officials cannot be absolved of accountability
She believes 99% accuracy is already legally mandatory
practiceQuestions.explanation: "Quand bien même... ne saurait dispenser..." firmly upholds human public accountability regardless of technical reliability.

lesson.checkpointModelAnswer: Une centralisation précipitée de nos procédures d’évaluation ne serait pas sans susciter des tensions durables sur le terrain. Les rapports d’audit ont beau vanter les économies d’échelle promises sur le papier, l’efficacité comptable à court terme ne saurait justifier la perte d’autonomie pédagogique des équipes locales. Quand bien même une plateforme unifiée permettrait de harmoniser certains indicateurs statistiques, il n’est pas exclu qu’elle appauvrisse la richesse des initiatives adaptées à chaque territoire. Permettez-moi donc de suggérer une voie médiane : définir un socle commun d’exigences transparentes tout en laissant aux établissements une marge réelle d’expérimentation évaluée dans la durée.

modules.title: Literary Tenses (Passé Simple), Idioms & Cultural Allusions
modules.summary: Read classic and contemporary French literature, historical journalism, and nuanced cultural commentary with zero friction.
objectives: Recognize all Passé Simple patterns (-a/-èrent, -it/-irent, -ut/-urent, fut, eut, fit, vint) effortlessly in novels and prestige press.
Decode high-frequency Francophone cultural idioms and allusions (un coup d’épée dans l’eau, la quadrature du cercle, un serpent de mer, botter en touche).
Track subtle irony, historical references, and register shifts inside dense C2 literary/editorial excerpts.
grammarCheckpoints: Press & intellectual idioms (serpent de mer, quadrature du cercle)

drills.title: Le Monde Cultural Idiom & Passé Simple Decode
drills.instruction: Read the passage and unpack the exact meaning of "serpent de mer", "fût-ce", and "botter en touche".
drills.samplePassage: La réforme fiscale fait figure de véritable serpent de mer : dès qu’elle revint à l’ordre du jour, plusieurs ministres préférèrent botter en touche, refusant d’arbitrer fût-ce à la marge.

drills.title: France Culture Cultural Debate Analysis
drills.instruction: Listen and catch the idiomatic metaphors used to criticize the stalled infrastructure bill.
drills.audioScript: Réconcilier baisse des impôts, gratuité totale et équilibre budgétaire relève de la quadrature du cercle ; sans arbitrage courageux, ce plan risque fort de n’être qu’un coup d’épée dans l’eau.

modules.checkpointPrompt: Write a 125-word cultural commentary analyzing a recurring public debate using at least three C2 idioms ("serpent de mer", "quadrature du cercle", "fût-ce", "botter en touche").

lesson.overview: Unlock effortless comprehension of French novels, prestige journalism, and intellectual radio by mastering literary verb cues and cultural metaphors.

sections.heading: Passé Simple & Surviving Subjonctif Imparfait Gems
sections.explanation: You rarely speak in the Passé Simple, yet it fills French novels, biographies, and prestige journalism (il parla, ils répondirent, elle sut, il fut, ils eurent, elle vint). Meanwhile, two Subjonctif Imparfait gems survive actively in modern C2 prose and speech: "fût-ce" (even if only / be it only) and "eût-il fallu" (had it been necessary).
sections.formula: -ER: -a / -èrent  |  -IR/-RE: -it / -irent  |  -U group: fut, eut, put, sut, voulut  |  "fût-ce" = même si ce n’est que

examples.target: Lorsque la réforme fut promulguée, elle suscita d’emblée des débats passionnés qui durèrent une décennie.
examples.translation: When the reform was enacted, it immediately sparked passionate debates that lasted a decade.

examples.target: Il convient d’écouter toutes les parties, fût-ce pour constater un désaccord fécond.
examples.translation: It is advisable to listen to all parties, even if only to note a fruitful disagreement.

sections.proTip: Using "fût-ce" once naturally in a DALF C2 essay ("fût-ce de manière transitoire") signals effortless near-native stylistic poise!

sections.heading: Press & Intellectual Idioms Every C2 Reader Must Know
sections.explanation: French journalists and radio commentators rely on vivid recurring metaphors. Memorize the top C2 editorial idioms so their implicit irony never slips past you.
sections.formula: un serpent de mer (recurring unresolved issue) · botter en touche (dodge/evade) · la quadrature du cercle (impossible dilemma)

examples.target: La réforme des rythmes scolaires est un serpent de mer politique sur lequel beaucoup préfèrent botter en touche.
examples.translation: School-schedule reform is a recurring political chestnut that many prefer to sidestep.
examples.highlight: serpent de mer ... botter en touche

examples.target: Sans sanction crédible, cette charte volontaire risque de demeurer un coup d’épée dans l’eau.
examples.translation: Without credible sanctions, this voluntary charter risks remaining a futile exercise.

sections.proTip: Watch sports metaphors in French politics: "botter en touche" comes from rugby (kicking the ball out of bounds to avoid confrontation)!

vocabCards.example: L’harmonisation fiscale européenne reste un vieux serpent de mer.
vocabCards.exampleNote: Ubiquitous in French political journalism.

vocabCards.meaning: squaring the circle / an impossible task
vocabCards.example: Concilier hyper-croissance et zéro émission ressemble à la quadrature du cercle.
vocabCards.exampleNote: Notice pronunciation [kwa-], NOT [ka-].

vocabCards.meaning: to dodge / sidestep a thorny question
vocabCards.example: Interrogé sur le déficit, le porte-parole a habilement botté en touche.
vocabCards.exampleNote: Rugby metaphor used across press & debate.

vocabCards.meaning: even if only / were it only
vocabCards.example: Rien ne justifie un tel recul, fût-ce à titre provisoire.
vocabCards.exampleNote: Living C2 gem from Subjonctif Imparfait of être.

vocabCards.example: Cette campagne sans moyens s’est révélée un coup d’épée dans l’eau.
vocabCards.exampleNote: Literally "a sword blow in water".

practiceQuestions.prompt: In Le Monde, "Interrogé sur le financement, le ministre a botté en touche" means:
options: He gave a detailed budgetary breakdown.
He evaded answering the sensitive question directly.
He resigned immediately during the interview.
practiceQuestions.explanation: "Botter en touche" is an idiomatic metaphor meaning to sidestep or dodge an awkward question.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which verb is the Passé Simple of "savoir" in "Elle sut immédiatement saisir l’occasion"?
practiceQuestions.explanation: "Il/elle sut" is the Passé Simple of "savoir" ("she knew how to / managed to").

practiceQuestions.prompt: Listen to the commentator. What is his verdict on the proposed plan?
practiceQuestions.audioScript: Réconcilier baisse des impôts, gratuité totale et équilibre budgétaire relève de la quadrature du cercle ; sans arbitrage courageux, ce plan risque fort de n’être qu’un coup d’épée dans l’eau.
options: It reconciles all three goals smoothly
Its contradictory promises look impossible and risk achieving nothing without hard choices
It has already balanced the national budget
practiceQuestions.explanation: "Quadrature du cercle" (impossible dilemma) + "coup d’épée dans l’eau" (futile effort) convey sharp skepticism.

lesson.checkpointModelAnswer: Depuis plus de vingt ans, la refonte des rythmes scolaires fait figure de véritable serpent de mer dans le débat éducatif francophone. À chaque rentrée, des commissions spécialisées publient des diagnostics convergents, tandis que les décideurs successifs préfèrent trop souvent botter en touche face aux résistances corporatistes ou logistiques. Il faut reconnaître que concilier l’intérêt chronobiologique des enfants, les contraintes horaires des familles actives et les budgets municipaux relève parfois de la quadrature du cercle. Pourtant, renoncer à expérimenter — fût-ce à l’échelle de quelques territoires pilotes rigoureusement évalués — condamnerait les rapports futurs à n’être qu’un nouveau coup d’épée dans l’eau, laissant intactes des inégalités d’apprentissage que chacun déplore en parole.

modules.title: DALF C2 Integrated Writing: Dossier Synthesis Into Publication Prose
modules.summary: Master the flagship 3.5-hour DALF C2 written production: weaving a 2,000-word multi-source dossier into a cohesive 700-word article, report, or speech.
objectives: Mine a 2,000-word dossier systematically into a 3-axis strategic plan without ever losing your personal editorial voice.
Integrate dossier data, conflicting perspectives, and original counter-examples smoothly without mechanical "Document 1 says...".
Match publication-grade genre conventions (editorial chronique, rapport ministériel, discours inaugural).
grammarCheckpoints: Seamless source integration without verbatim copying
Genre-authentic framing (article de fond / rapport / discours)

drills.title: 3-Document Dossier Rapid Synthesis Matrix
drills.instruction: Extract the core tension and 3 cross-cutting themes from a multi-angle brief on universal basic cultural passes.
drills.samplePassage: Source A : Le pass culture élargit la fréquentation des librairies mais profite surtout aux jeunes déjà sensibilisés. Source B : Les médiateurs scolaires soulignent que sans accompagnement collectif en classe, les écarts socio-géographiques persistent.

drills.title: DALF C2 Editorial Lead & Section Transition Lab
drills.instruction: Draft a publication-grade headline, lead paragraph, and two seamlessly integrated analytical paragraphs (250 words).

modules.checkpointPrompt: Write a 130-word publication-grade excerpt for a review of ideas integrating both positive findings and sociological limits of a youth cultural pass, ending with a concrete policy recommendation.

lesson.overview: Learn how DALF C2 Écrit transcends DALF C1: instead of separating summary and essay, you fuse rigorous dossier mastery into one seamless, publication-ready piece.

sections.heading: Fusing Dossier Mastery With Authoritative Personal Voice
sections.explanation: Unlike DALF C1 (separate neutral Synthèse + Essai), DALF C2 asks for ONE substantial, real-world genre text (700+ words: feature article, policy report, conference speech) that integrates the dossier’s facts organically while advancing your own compelling argument. Never write "Comme le dit le texte 2" — weave ideas naturally ("Les évaluations récentes corroborent ce constat...").
sections.formula: Genre Framing (Title/Role) -> Contextualized Problem -> Organic Dossier Weaving + Original Insights -> Strategic Recommendations

examples.target: Plusieurs enquêtes de terrain corroborent ce paradoxe : l’incitation financière individuelle profite d’abord aux publics déjà familiers des lieux culturels.
examples.translation: Several field surveys corroborate this paradox: individual financial incentives first benefit audiences already familiar with cultural venues.

examples.target: Mettre ces chiffres en perspective permet de dépasser la querelle idéologique et de préconiser un accompagnement collectif dès le collège.
examples.translation: Putting these figures into perspective allows moving beyond ideological quarrels and recommending collective guidance from middle school.
examples.highlight: Mettre ces chiffres en perspective ... préconiser

sections.proTip: Match visual layout to the requested genre! An article de fond needs a striking headline + subheadings; a rapport needs a formal title, numbered recommendations, and crisp executive tone.

sections.heading: Precision Verbs for Attributing & Evaluating Sources
sections.explanation: Replace flat "dire / montrer" with sharp intellectual verbs that signal your analytical stance: "corroborer" (confirm with evidence), "infirmer" (disprove), "nuancer" (qualify), "mettre en lumière" (illuminate), "préconiser" (advocate/recommend formally).
sections.formula: Confirm: corroborer / étayer  |  Challenge: infirmer / relativiser  |  Recommend: préconiser / plaider pour

examples.target: Loin d’étayer la thèse d’un désintérêt des jeunes pour la lecture, les statistiques mettent en lumière de nouveaux usages hybrides.
examples.translation: Far from substantiating the thesis of youth disinterest in reading, statistics bring to light new hybrid habits.

examples.target: Aussi préconisons-nous de rééquilibrer le dispositif entre crédit individuel et sorties scolaires financées.
examples.translation: Therefore we recommend rebalancing the scheme between individual credit and funded school outings.

sections.proTip: Verify every single quantitative fact you cite against the dossier so your synthesis remains 100% faithful as well as stylish!

vocabCards.meaning: an op-ed column / recurring feature article
vocabCards.example: Dans sa chronique hebdomadaire, elle interroge nos habitudes numériques.
vocabCards.exampleNote: Frequent DALF C2 target genre.

vocabCards.example: Ce rapport préconise une refonte progressive de la gouvernance.
vocabCards.exampleNote: Calls for structured headings and crisp impartiality.

vocabCards.meaning: to put into broader context / perspective
vocabCards.example: Il importe de mettre en perspective ces résultats sur dix ans.
vocabCards.exampleNote: Signals C2 analytical altitude.

vocabCards.example: Les données régionales corroborent les conclusions de l’observatoire.
vocabCards.exampleNote: Elevated substitute for "confirmer".

vocabCards.example: Les experts préconisent un financement pluriannuel transparent.
vocabCards.exampleNote: Never use "à" — directly transitive ("préconiser une réforme").

practiceQuestions.prompt: What is the key structural difference between DALF C1 Writing and DALF C2 Integrated Writing?
options: DALF C2 forbids using any information from the dossier.
DALF C2 fuses dossier synthesis and personal argumentation into one cohesive genre piece (article, report, speech) rather than two separate tasks.
DALF C2 only requires a 100-word informal postcard.
practiceQuestions.explanation: DALF C2 tests integrated mastery: weaving dossier content seamlessly into an authoritative, genre-accurate piece of 700+ words.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which verb means "to disprove / invalidate a claim with counter-evidence"?
practiceQuestions.explanation: "Infirmer" (to invalidate/refute) is the exact antonym of "confirmer / corroborer".

practiceQuestions.prompt: How should you reference dossier findings in a DALF C2 feature article?
options: Write "Dans le document 1, ligne 14, l’auteur dit..."
Integrate the data seamlessly into your prose ("Les enquêtes de terrain corroborent ce constat...").
Copy entire paragraphs verbatim in quotation marks.
practiceQuestions.explanation: Natural, publication-grade integration without clunky "Document 1" labels or verbatim copying is essential at C2.

lesson.checkpointModelAnswer:
Démocratiser la culture : au-delà du seul chèque individuel

Conçu pour lever la barrière financière qui éloigne nombre de jeunes des librairies, salles de spectacle et musées, le dispositif du pass culturel individuel affiche à première vue un bilan quantitatif flatteur. Les études d’impact récentes corroborent en effet une fréquentation accrue des commerces culturels par les bénéficiaires. Toutefois, mettre ces chiffres en perspective révèle une limite sociologique tenace : la subvention directe profite prioritairement aux adolescents déjà familiarisés avec ces pratiques dans leur cadre familial, tandis que l’éloignement géographique et l’autocensure symbolique persistent ailleurs. Aussi préconisons-nous de rééquilibrer résolument le budget vers la part collective — médiation artistique en classe, sorties encadrées et résidences d’auteurs en zone rurale — afin que l’accès matériel s’accompagne enfin d’une véritable émancipation culturelle.

modules.title: Executive Oral Synthesis & Critical Audio Compte Rendu (DALF C2)
modules.summary: Distill a 15-minute authentic French radio broadcast into a razor-sharp 6-minute oral compte rendu followed by an independent thesis.
objectives: Distinguish the two halves of DALF C2 Oral: Part 1 faithful thematic compte rendu vs. Part 2 original argued stance.
Capture speaker hierarchy, subtle concessions, and rhetorical tone across 15 minutes of fast unscripted Francophone debate.
Transition seamlessly from objective reporting into your own bold intellectual position.
grammarCheckpoints: Reporting multiple voices cleanly without monotony
Signaled transition from compte rendu to prise de position

drills.title: Multi-Speaker Radio Broadcast Axis Capture
drills.instruction: Listen and map the shared premise, the point of friction, and the unstated assumption ("en filigrane").
drills.audioScript: Animatrice: Nos deux invités partagent un constat clair sur le vieillissement démographique. En revanche, tandis que Monsieur Girard plaide pour le maintien à domicile connecté, Madame Laurent s’en démarque en alertant sur la solitude affective que nul capteur ne compense.

drills.title: 3-Minute Compte Rendu + Pivot Sprint
drills.instruction: Deliver a concise, objective synthesis of a debate and execute a crisp spoken pivot into your own nuanced thesis.

modules.checkpointPrompt: Deliver a 130-word oral compte rendu + pivot synthesizing two contrasting perspectives on aging-in-place technology and launching your own argued thesis.

lesson.overview: Master the toughest listening-to-speaking integration in French certification: turning a long live broadcast into a crystalline executive briefing and personal position.

sections.heading: Part 1: The High-Altitude Compte Rendu (Zero Chronological Ramble)
sections.explanation: Never narrate a 15-minute podcast minute-by-minute ("D’abord l’animatrice a dit..., puis à la cinquième minute..."). Reorganize the recording by INTELLECTUAL ARCHITECTURE: central question -> shared diagnostic -> lines of divergence -> implicit stakes ("en filigrane"). Stay 100% faithful without injecting your own opinion yet!
sections.formula: Context & Core Issue -> Constat partagé -> Lignes de fracture (A vs. B) -> Enjeux en filigrane

examples.target: Les lignes de force de cette émission s’articulent autour d’un constat partagé mais de remèdes radicalement opposés.
examples.translation: The main thrusts of this broadcast revolve around a shared diagnosis yet radically opposite remedies.

examples.target: En filigrane se dessine une interrogation plus profonde sur la place accordée au lien humain dans le soin.
examples.translation: Beneath the surface emerges a deeper question about the place given to human connection in care.

sections.proTip: Explicitly flag your transition between Part 1 and Part 2: "Après avoir restitué les lignes de force de ce débat, je souhaiterais à présent prendre position sur..."

sections.heading: Part 2: Stepping Boldly Into Your Original Prise de Position
sections.explanation: Once your compte rendu concludes, step out from behind the speakers! You are given a specific angle/mission (e.g., advising a ministry, speaking at a symposium). Take a clear, nuanced, well-illustrated stance that builds on the audio without simply echoing one guest.
sections.formula: Explicit Pivot -> Clear Personal Thesis -> 2 Deepened Axes (Fresh Examples) -> Memorable Synthesis

examples.target: Tout en souscrivant à la prudence de l’intervenante, je me démarque d’une opposition figée entre technique et humanité.
examples.translation: While endorsing the speaker’s caution, I part ways with a rigid opposition between technology and humanity.
examples.highlight: Tout en souscrivant à ... je me démarque de

examples.target: Ce que le débat laisse curieusement de côté, c’est le rôle décisif de l’architecture intergénérationnelle.
examples.translation: What the debate curiously leaves aside is the decisive role of intergenerational housing design.

sections.proTip: Noting a blind spot ("ce que les intervenants abordent peu...") is a supreme DALF C2 move that proves genuine critical autonomy!

vocabCards.meaning: the main lines / overarching structure of an argument
vocabCards.example: Je dégagerai d’abord les lignes de force de cette table ronde.
vocabCards.exampleNote: Ideal opener for DALF C2 oral synthesis.

vocabCards.meaning: between the lines / implicitly beneath the surface
vocabCards.example: En filigrane apparaît une inquiétude générationnelle profonde.
vocabCards.exampleNote: Watermark metaphor for reading implicit meaning.

vocabCards.meaning: to distance oneself from / stand apart from
vocabCards.example: La sociologue se démarque nettement de cette lecture purement économique.
vocabCards.exampleNote: Crisp verb for mapping disagreement.

vocabCards.example: Malgré leurs désaccords, tous partent d’un constat partagé.
vocabCards.exampleNote: Anchor point for structuring multi-speaker synthesis.

vocabCards.meaning: to take a stand / articulate one’s position
vocabCards.example: Permettez-moi à présent de prendre position sur cette réforme.
vocabCards.exampleNote: Clean verbal boundary into Part 2.

practiceQuestions.prompt: What is the biggest mistake candidates make during Part 1 (compte rendu) of the DALF C2 Oral?
options: Grouping arguments thematically into shared ground and points of tension.
Narrating the broadcast chronologically minute-by-minute and mixing in personal opinion too early.
Flagging clearly when they transition from objective synthesis to personal stance.
practiceQuestions.explanation: A C2 compte rendu must be thematically restructured and strictly faithful before clearly pivoting to personal argument.

practiceQuestions.prompt: What does "en filigrane" signify in critical French analysis?
options: Implicitly present beneath the surface / between the lines
practiceQuestions.explanation: "En filigrane" (like a paper watermark) points to subtle underlying themes or unstated assumptions.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Listen to the debate summary. Why does Madame Laurent distance herself from Monsieur Girard’s proposal?
practiceQuestions.audioScript: Animatrice: Nos deux invités partagent un constat clair sur le vieillissement démographique. En revanche, tandis que Monsieur Girard plaide pour le maintien à domicile connecté, Madame Laurent s’en démarque en alertant sur la solitude affective que nul capteur ne compense.
options: Because sensors are illegal in France
Because connected home sensors cannot compensate for emotional loneliness
Because she denies demographic aging is occurring
practiceQuestions.explanation: Madame Laurent warns against "la solitude affective que nul capteur ne compense".

lesson.checkpointModelAnswer: Les lignes de force de cet échange s’organisent autour d’un constat partagé — l’accélération du vieillissement démographique — mais d’une divergence nette sur les réponses à privilégier. Tandis que le premier intervenant met en avant les capteurs connectés pour sécuriser le maintien à domicile, son interlocutrice s’en démarque en rappelant que nul dispositif technique ne comble l’isolement affectif. En filigrane se pose la question de la place même des aînés dans la cité. Après ce compte rendu, je souhaite prendre position : il serait stérile d’opposer innovation domestique et présence humaine. Ce que le débat aborde peu, c’est l’habitat partagé intergénérationnel, où la domotique libère précisément les soignants des tâches répétitives pour leur redonner du temps relationnel véritable.

modules.title: High-Stakes Jury Sparring, Register Agility & DALF C2 Pinnacle
modules.summary: Demonstrate complete near-native agility across registers, subtle humor, spontaneous repartee, and full DALF C2 exam performance.
objectives: Shift effortlessly across academic, diplomatic, journalistic, and lightly humorous spoken registers according to audience.
Parry rapid, provocative DALF C2 jury interruptions without losing precision, poise, or syntactic complexity.
Complete full integrated DALF C2 simulations consistently above 70%.

drills.title: DALF C2 Rapid-Fire Jury Provocation Gauntlet
drills.instruction: Answer 4 sharp, ironic jury challenges in 45 seconds each while maintaining C2 flow, precision, and wit.

drills.title: Full DALF C2 Integrated Timed Dress Rehearsal
drills.instruction: Complete the LinguaVerve French C2 Simulated Exam under Strict Pressure Mode across all 4 modules.

modules.checkpointPrompt: Deliver a 135-word C2 closing debate statement responding with poise and nuance to a jury claiming that global English makes multilingual education obsolete.

lesson.overview: Polish the final 5% separating advanced fluency from true C2 command: effortless spontaneity, register agility, and intellectual grace under pressure.

sections.heading: Spontaneous Repartee & Graceful Self-Correction Under Pressure
sections.explanation: True C2 mastery does NOT mean sounding like a stiff textbook! During the final 10-minute DALF C2 debate, examiners look for lively, responsive dialogue — acknowledging an examiner’s irony with a smile ("À vrai dire, votre provocation touche juste..."), sharpening a claim dynamically ("d’autant plus que..."), and bringing concrete cultural depth.
sections.formula: Witty acknowledgment ("À vrai dire...") -> Sharpened reinforcement ("d’autant plus que...") -> Principle ("En dernier ressort...")

examples.target: À vrai dire, l’argument utilitariste séduit au premier abord, d’autant plus que la traduction instantanée progresse à vue d’œil.
examples.translation: To tell the truth, the utilitarian argument appeals at first glance, all the more so as instant translation improves visibly.
examples.highlight: À vrai dire ... d’autant plus que

examples.target: En dernier ressort, la maîtrise d’une langue offre une intimité culturelle sans commune mesure avec une traduction médiatisée.
examples.translation: Ultimately, mastering a language offers a cultural intimacy beyond compare with mediated translation.
examples.highlight: En dernier ressort ... sans commune mesure

sections.proTip: If you realize mid-sentence you want a sharper word, refine yourself cleanly like a native speaker: "— ou plus exactement, pour nuancer mon propos —". That actually raises your C2 score!

sections.heading: Register Agility & Final DALF C2 Excellence Checklist
sections.explanation: Know when to deploy a punchy idiom ("un pari risqué", "un trompe-l’œil") alongside high syntax ("aussi convient-il", "quand bien même"). Before submitting any C2 writing, run a 10-minute surgical pass: eliminate noun repetitions via synonyms/pronouns, verify past-participle agreements, check every subjunctive trigger, and polish the opening hook and closing cadence.
sections.formula: C2 Polish Pass: 1) Lexical variety -> 2) Subjonctif & Participle agreement -> 3) Transitions & Cadence

examples.target: Miser sur le tout-technologique sans investir dans les humanités constituerait un pari risqué pour nos sociétés.
examples.translation: Betting everything on technology without investing in the humanities would be a risky gamble for our societies.

examples.target: Reste à savoir si nos institutions sauront saisir cette opportunité avant que le débat ne se referme.
examples.translation: It remains to be seen whether our institutions will seize this opportunity before the debate closes.

sections.proTip: Opening a concluding sentence with compact "Reste à savoir si..." (= Il reste à savoir si...) gives both written essays and spoken debates an unmistakable native French finish!

vocabCards.meaning: to tell the truth / candidly speaking
vocabCards.example: À vrai dire, cette apparente contradiction mérite d’être creusée.
vocabCards.exampleNote: Natural conversational poise in high-level debates.

vocabCards.meaning: all the more so since / especially as
vocabCards.example: Le défi est urgent, d’autant plus que les échéances se rapprochent.
vocabCards.exampleNote: Notice pronounced final "s" [plys] in "d’autant plus que"!

vocabCards.meaning: beyond compare / out of all proportion
vocabCards.example: Les enjeux actuels sont sans commune mesure avec ceux du siècle passé.
vocabCards.exampleNote: High-impact C2 comparative idiom.

vocabCards.example: Négliger la formation des enseignants serait un pari risqué.
vocabCards.exampleNote: Vivid yet fully appropriate in executive French.

vocabCards.example: En dernier ressort, c’est aux citoyens qu’appartient l’arbitrage.
vocabCards.exampleNote: Legal/philosophical precision phrase.

practiceQuestions.prompt: How is "plus" pronounced in the phrase "d’autant plus que"?
practiceQuestions.explanation: In "d’autant plus que", "de plus", and positive comparisons meaning "more", the final "s" of "plus" is pronounced [plys].

practiceQuestions.prompt: What does "En dernier ressort, l’arbitrage relève du débat démocratique" convey?
options: As a trivial afterthought, democracy might comment.
Ultimately / in the final instance, the decisive judgment belongs to democratic debate.
Democratic debate was rejected at the last resort.
practiceQuestions.explanation: "En dernier ressort" (borrowed from law: court of final appeal) means "in the final analysis / ultimately".

practiceQuestions.prompt: Listen to the closing remark. What final caution does the speaker leave with the jury?
practiceQuestions.audioScript: À vrai dire, renoncer à l’enseignement des langues sous prétexte que des algorithmes traduisent instantanément serait un pari risqué ; en dernier ressort, comprendre l’autre dans sa propre langue crée une confiance sans commune mesure avec n’importe quel outil.
options: That instant translators should be outlawed in schools
That abandoning language education is a risky gamble because direct dialogue builds unmatched trust
That only diplomats need to learn foreign languages
practiceQuestions.explanation: She calls abandoning language learning "un pari risqué" because understanding someone directly builds trust "sans commune mesure" with any tool.

lesson.checkpointModelAnswer: À vrai dire, la tentation du monolinguisme utilitaire séduit par sa simplicité apparente, d’autant plus que les outils de traduction simultanée atteignent une fluidité impressionnante dans les échanges techniques. Toutefois, en déduire que l’éducation plurilingue deviendrait superflue constituerait un pari risqué sur le plan intellectuel comme géopolitique. Une langue n’est pas un simple code interchangeable que l’on transposerait mot à mot : elle porte une mémoire historique, des nuances d’humour, d’implicite et de politesse dont la maîtrise directe forge une confiance sans commune mesure avec une conversation filtrée par une machine. Quand bien même l’anglais demeurerait une passerelle commode, renoncer à la pluralité des langues appauvrirait notre capacité collective à penser autrement. En dernier ressort, apprendre une langue étrangère reste l’école la plus exigeante — et la plus vivante — de l’altérité.

intensiveCourses.title: Japanese A1 / JLPT N5 Zero-to-Survival Launchpad
intensiveCourses.subtitle: Decode Hiragana, Katakana, mora rhythm, foundational particles (は・が・を・に・で), polite です/ます verbs, and essential Te-form survival requests.
intensiveCourses.passingCriteria: JLPT N5 scaled score ≥ 80/180 (min 38/120 Language Knowledge & Reading, 19/60 Listening) + 4-skill survival output.

examBlueprint.reading: 50 mins · Kana & ~100 basic kanji recognition, short notices, café signs, schedules, and 120-character emails.
examBlueprint.listening: 30 mins · Slow, clear Tokyo everyday dialogues on prices, train times, shopping, and simple requests.
examBlueprint.writing: 25 mins · Clean kana/basic kanji short messages, self-introductions, and daily routine paragraphs (60–120 chars).
examBlueprint.speaking: 8 mins · Self-introduction, ordering food, asking directions, and polite survival requests with 〜てください.

modules.title: Hiragana, Katakana, Mora Timing & First Introductions
modules.summary: Lock in equal-beat mora timing (long vowels & small っ), read Hiragana and Katakana effortlessly, and introduce yourself politely with は・です・か.
objectives: Read and write core Hiragana/Katakana syllables including voiced (だ/ば/ぱ) and contracted (きゃ/しょ) sounds.
Introduce your name, nationality, and occupation naturally with 「はじめまして。〜と申します / 〜です」.
Form polite affirmative, negative (じゃありません), and yes/no questions (か).
grammarCheckpoints: Topic particle は (wa) & copula です
Negative じゃありません & Question marker か
Possessive/linking particle の (N1 の N2)
keyVocabulary: よろしくおねがいします

drills.title: Mora & Self-Introduction Ear Drill
drills.instruction: Listen carefully for long vowels and capture the speaker’s name, country, and job.
drills.audioScript: はじめまして。エマです。カナダから来ました。東京の会社員です。どうぞよろしくおねがいします。

drills.title: 45-Second Polite Self-Introduction
drills.instruction: Introduce your name, country, current city, occupation, and closing greeting with even mora timing.

modules.checkpointPrompt: Record or write a polite Japanese self-introduction covering your name, country, occupation, and a polite closing.

lesson.overview: Build clean Tokyo Japanese pronunciation from day one by mastering mora-timed kana reading and the foundational 「X は Y です」 sentence frame.

sections.heading: The Core Identity Frame: X は Y です / じゃありません / か
sections.explanation: Japanese places the copula です at the very end of the sentence. Particle は (written ha, pronounced "wa") marks the topic ("As for X"). Add か at the end to turn any statement into a question — no word-order flip needed!
sections.formula: [Topic] は [Noun] です (is)  |  じゃありません (is not)  |  〜ですか (is it ~?)

examples.target: 私はカナダの会社員です。
examples.translation: I am an office worker from Canada.

examples.target: 田中さんは学生ですか。— いいえ、学生じゃありません。先生です。
examples.translation: Is Tanaka a student? — No, he is not a student. He is a teacher.
examples.highlight: ですか / じゃありません

sections.proTip: Never add a question mark AND drop か in polite Japanese; in standard writing, か already functions as the spoken question marker.

sections.heading: Mora Rhythm, Long Vowels & Particle の
sections.explanation: Every kana counts as one equal beat (mora): おばあさん (5 beats, grandmother) vs. おばさん (4 beats, aunt). Meanwhile, particle の connects two nouns from general to specific: 「日本語の先生」(Japanese-language teacher).
sections.formula: Noun 1 (modifier) + の + Noun 2 (main noun)

examples.target: さくら大学の日本語の学生です。
examples.translation: I am a Japanese-language student at Sakura University.

examples.target: これは私のコーヒーです。
examples.translation: This is my coffee. (Hold コー and ヒー for 2 beats each!)

sections.proTip: When reading Katakana loanwords, the dash ー always extends the previous vowel by one full mora beat (コーヒー = ko-o-hi-i).

vocabCards.example: はじめまして。ケンジです。
vocabCards.exampleNote: Used only the very first time you meet someone.

vocabCards.example: 私は大学の学生です。
vocabCards.exampleNote: Pronounced gakusē (long e sound).

vocabCards.example: 母は東京の会社員です。
vocabCards.exampleNote: General profession word; use 社員 with a specific company name.

vocabCards.example: 毎日、日本語を勉強します。
vocabCards.exampleNote: Add 語 (go) to country names for languages (英語, フランス語).

vocabCards.term: よろしくおねがいします
vocabCards.pronunciation: よろしくおねがいします (yoroshiku onegaishimasu)
vocabCards.meaning: Pleased to meet you / I look forward to working with you
vocabCards.example: これからどうぞよろしくおねがいします。
vocabCards.exampleNote: Essential social anchor at the end of introductions.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which sentence correctly means "Maria is a university student"?
options: マリアさんは大学の学生です。
マリアさんは学生の大学です。
マリアさんの大学は学生かです。
practiceQuestions.explanation: Particle の places the modifier first: 大学の学生 = student of a university.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Listen to the introduction. Where is Emma from and what is her job?
practiceQuestions.audioScript: はじめまして。エマです。カナダから来ました。東京の会社員です。どうぞよろしくおねがいします。
practiceQuestions.explanation: She says 「カナダから来ました」(came from Canada) and 「東京の会社員です」(company employee in Tokyo).

practiceQuestions.prompt: How do you politely say "I am not a teacher"?
options: 私は先生じゃありません。
practiceQuestions.explanation: Polite negative of です is じゃありません (or ではありません in formal writing).

lesson.checkpointModelAnswer: はじめまして。アレックスです。アメリカから来ました。今は東京に住んでいます。ＩＴの会社員です。日本語の勉強が大好きです。これからどうぞよろしくおねがいします。

modules.title: Numbers, Clock Times, Prices & Ordering with ください
modules.summary: Decode Japanese prices (円), clock times (〜時〜分), days of the week, and smooth café/konbini ordering using これ・それ・あれ and 〜をください.
objectives: Understand prices up to 10,000 yen (百・千・万) and phonetic shifts (三百 sanbyaku, 六百 roppyaku, 八百 happyaku).
Read store business hours and train departure times accurately.
Order items politely using これ/それ/あれ and basic counters (一つ・二つ・三つ).
grammarCheckpoints: Demonstratives これ・それ・あれ / この・その・あの
Clock times (〜時〜分) & から〜まで ranges
Polite ordering: [Item] を [Counter] ください

drills.title: Convenience Store Price Check
drills.instruction: Listen and write down what the customer orders and the total price in yen.
drills.audioScript: すみません、このサンドイッチを一つと、熱いお茶を二つください。はい、ぜんぶで六百八十円になります。

drills.title: Bakery Notice Scan
drills.instruction: Scan the bakery notice to check open days and opening time.
drills.samplePassage: みどりパン屋：営業時間 8:30〜19:00。水曜日は休みです。メロンパンは一つ220円です。

modules.checkpointPrompt: Write a short dialogue ordering two items at a café and asking the price and closing time.

lesson.overview: Master practical Japanese numbers, yen prices, business-hour notices, and demonstrative pronouns so you can shop and eat anywhere in Japan.

sections.heading: こ・そ・あ Demonstratives & Ordering with 〜をください
sections.explanation: Japanese divides space into three zones: こ (near speaker: これ / このN), そ (near listener: それ / そのN), and あ (far from both: あれ / あのN). Pair them with をください to order cleanly.
sections.formula: これ / この[Noun] を [Quantity] ください  |  これはいくらですか (How much is this?)

examples.target: すみません、そのケーキを二つください。
examples.translation: Excuse me, please give me two of those cakes (near the clerk).
examples.highlight: そのケーキを二つください

examples.target: あのコーヒーはいくらですか。— 四百五十円です。
examples.translation: How much is that coffee over there? — It is 450 yen.

sections.proTip: Remember: これ/それ/あれ stand ALONE ("this one"), whereas この/その/あの MUST be followed directly by a noun ("this cake").

sections.heading: Telling Time, Days & Schedule Ranges (から〜まで)
sections.explanation: Watch irregular clock readings: 4時 (よじ, NOT しじ), 7時 (しちじ), 9時 (くじ). For minutes, 分 toggles between ふん and ぷん (1分 いっぷん, 3分 さんぷん, 5分 ごふん, 10分 じゅっぷん). Connect open/close times with から (from) and まで (until).
sections.formula: [Start] から [End] まで (from ... until ...)  |  [Day] は休みです (closed on ...)

examples.target: 図書館は午前九時から午後六時までです。
examples.translation: The library is open from 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m.

examples.target: 月曜日は休みですが、日曜日は開いています。
examples.translation: It is closed on Mondays, but open on Sundays.

sections.proTip: In JLPT N5 listening, 300 (さんびゃく), 600 (ろっぴゃく), and 800 (はっぴゃく) appear constantly — drill them aloud!

vocabCards.example: このりんごは一ついくらですか。
vocabCards.exampleNote: Always asks price, never quantity (quantity uses いくつ).

vocabCards.meaning: please give me (noun + をください)
vocabCards.example: お水を一つください。
vocabCards.exampleNote: The #1 survival phrase in restaurants and shops.

vocabCards.pronunciation: えいぎょうじかん (eigyō jikan)
vocabCards.example: 営業時間は十時から八時までです。
vocabCards.exampleNote: Seen on virtually every Japanese storefront and website.

vocabCards.example: ぜんぶで千二百円です。
vocabCards.exampleNote: Pronounced "en" (no "y" sound in Japanese!).

vocabCards.example: 火曜日はお店の休みです。
vocabCards.exampleNote: On shop signs you will also see 定休日 (ていきゅうび).

practiceQuestions.prompt: Look at the sign: 「みどりパン屋：8:30〜19:00。水曜日は休みです。」 When can you buy bread?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Wednesday is closed and closing time is 19:00, so Thursday at 15:00 is open.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Listen to the shop clerk. How much is the total bill?
practiceQuestions.audioScript: すみません、このサンドイッチを一つと、熱いお茶を二つください。はい、ぜんぶで六百八十円になります。
practiceQuestions.explanation: 六百八十円 (roppyaku hachijū-en) equals 680 yen.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which sentence correctly asks "How much is this bag?"
options: これかばんはいくらですか。
このかばんはいくらですか。
このかばんをいくらですか。
practiceQuestions.explanation: Before a noun (かばん), use この (not これ), with topic particle は.

lesson.checkpointModelAnswer: すみません、このコーヒーはいくらですか。四百円です。じゃあ、熱いコーヒーを一つと、サンドイッチを二つください。ぜんぶで千円ですね。このお店は何時までですか。夜八時までです。ありがとうございます。

modules.title: Locations, Existence Verbs (あります・います) & Core Spatial Nouns
modules.summary: Pinpoint people and objects with います (animate) vs. あります (inanimate), spatial nouns (上・下・前・後ろ・隣), and exact location particle に.
objectives: Distinguish います (people, animals) from あります (buildings, objects, events).
Give clear neighborhood landmarks using 上・下・中・前・後ろ・隣・近く.
Ask where facilities are located with 「〜はどこですか / どこにありますか」.
grammarCheckpoints: あります (inanimate) vs. います (animate)
[Place] に [Thing/Person] が あります/います
Position words: の上・の下・の前・の隣・の間

drills.title: Station Map Landmarks Drill
drills.instruction: Read the short map description and find where the post office is located.
drills.samplePassage: 駅の前に大きい本屋があります。本屋の隣に銀行があります。郵便局は銀行とカフェの間にあります。

drills.title: Describe Your Desk & Neighborhood
drills.instruction: State 4 items on your desk and 2 places near your home using あります/います and position nouns.

modules.checkpointPrompt: Describe your room and neighborhood in Japanese using at least four location phrases (上・前・隣・近く).

lesson.overview: Navigate Japanese cities and describe rooms accurately by pairing existence verbs あります/います with spatial reference nouns.

sections.heading: Animate います vs. Inanimate あります
sections.explanation: Japanese splits "there is / exists" into two verbs: います for living creatures that move on their own (people, cats, dogs) and あります for everything else (buildings, furniture, plants, scheduled events). The static location takes particle に.
sections.formula: [Place] に [Thing] が あります  |  [Place] に [Person/Animal] が います

examples.target: 駅の近くに静かな公園があります。
examples.translation: There is a quiet park near the station.
examples.highlight: 近くに ... があります

examples.target: 公園の中に小さい犬が二匹います。
examples.translation: There are two small dogs inside the park.
examples.highlight: 中に ... が ... います

sections.proTip: Even if you say "I have a meeting tomorrow" or "I have a sister", Japanese uses existence: 「明日テストがあります」 / 「姉が一人います」.

sections.heading: Building Exact Directions with Spatial Nouns
sections.explanation: Spatial words like 上 (on/above), 下 (under), 前 (in front of), 後ろ (behind), 隣 (next to), and 間 (between) are NOUNS in Japanese — so they always connect to the landmark with の!
sections.formula: [Landmark] の [上 / 下 / 前 / 後ろ / 隣 / 近く] に

examples.target: 郵便局は銀行とカフェの間にあります。
examples.translation: The post office is between the bank and the café.

examples.target: すみません、切符売り場はどこにありますか。— 階段の右にあります。
examples.translation: Excuse me, where is the ticket office? — It is to the right of the stairs.

sections.proTip: Use 隣 (となり) only for things of the same category side by side (building next to building, person next to person); use 近く for general proximity.

vocabCards.meaning: to exist / there is (inanimate objects, places, events)
vocabCards.example: 机の上にノートがあります。
vocabCards.exampleNote: Negative polite: ありません.

vocabCards.example: 教室に先生がいます。
vocabCards.exampleNote: Negative polite: いません.

vocabCards.example: ホテルの隣にコンビニがあります。
vocabCards.exampleNote: Always linked with の: X の隣に.

vocabCards.example: 家の近くに大きいスーパーがあります。
vocabCards.exampleNote: Also used adverbially as 近くで for actions.

vocabCards.example: 新宿駅は東京にあります。
vocabCards.exampleNote: Core A1 travel kanji; combine with 前 → 駅前 (in front of the station).

practiceQuestions.prompt: 「本屋の隣に銀行があります。郵便局は銀行とカフェの間にあります。」 Where is the post office?
options: Between the bank and the café
practiceQuestions.explanation: 銀行とカフェの間 means "between the bank and the café".

practiceQuestions.prompt: Choose the grammatically correct sentence for "There is a cat under the table":
options: テーブルの下に猫があります。
テーブルの下に猫がいます。
テーブルの下で猫がいます。
practiceQuestions.explanation: A cat is animate (います), and static existence takes particle に (テーブルの下に).

practiceQuestions.prompt: Listen to the directions. Where is the pharmacy?
practiceQuestions.audioScript: すみません、薬局はどこにありますか。えっと、あの交差点の右に郵便局がありますね。薬局はその郵便局の隣です。
practiceQuestions.explanation: The speaker explains 「薬局はその郵便局の隣です」 (next to that post office).

lesson.checkpointModelAnswer: 私のアパートは駅の近くにあります。アパートの隣に小さいパン屋とコンビニがあります。部屋の中にベッドと机があります。机の上にパソコンと本があります。とても便利な場所です。

modules.title: Polite Verb Conjugation (ます・ません・ました) & Action Particles
modules.summary: Describe your full daily routine across present, future, and past tenses using polite ます verbs and core particles を・で・に・へ・と.
objectives: Conjugate any polite verb smoothly across all 4 tenses (ます / ません / ました / ませんでした).
Distinguish に (specific clock time / arrival) vs. で (action location / means of transport).
Write a cohesive 80-character diary entry describing yesterday’s schedule.
grammarCheckpoints: 4-way polite verb grid (ます / ません / ました / ませんでした)
Action location で vs. Time marker に vs. Direct object を
Companion particle と & frequency adverbs (毎日・よく・ときどき)

drills.title: Kenji’s Weekday Schedule
drills.instruction: Listen and note Kenji’s wake-up time, commuting method, and evening activity.
drills.audioScript: 私は毎朝六時半に起きます。朝ごはんを食べて、七時半に電車で会社へ行きます。夜は家で日本語の本を読みます。

drills.title: Yesterday’s Mini-Diary
drills.instruction: Write 5 sentences about what you did yesterday using past tense ました and at least 3 different particles.

modules.checkpointPrompt: Write a short Japanese diary entry describing your typical weekday morning and what you did yesterday evening.

lesson.overview: Unlock fluent daily storytelling by automating the 4 polite verb endings and locking in the exact roles of を, に, で, へ, and と.

sections.heading: The 4-Way Polite Verb Engine (ます・ません・ました・ませんでした)
sections.explanation: In Japanese, polite verbs do not change for I/you/he/she/they! You only mark Non-Past (present/future) vs. Past, and Affirmative vs. Negative. Swap the tail cleanly: 食べます (eat/will eat), 食べません (do not eat), 食べました (ate), 食べませんでした (did not eat).
sections.formula: Stem + ます (present/future) | ません (neg) | ました (past) | ませんでした (past neg)

examples.target: 今朝、コーヒーを飲みましたが、パンを食べませんでした。
examples.translation: This morning I drank coffee, but I did not eat bread.
examples.highlight: 飲みました / 食べませんでした

examples.target: 明日、友だちと京都へ行きます。
examples.translation: Tomorrow I will go to Kyoto with a friend.
examples.highlight: 友だちと ... へ行きます

sections.proTip: Relative time words like 今日 (today), 明日 (tomorrow), 昨日 (yesterday), and 毎日 (every day) NEVER take particle に! Only numbered times/days (7時に, 月曜日に) take に.

sections.heading: Action Stage で vs. Destination に/へ
sections.explanation: Always use で for the place where an activity happens (レストランで食べます) and for the vehicle/tool used (電車で行きます, はしで食べます). Use に or へ for destinations with movement verbs (行く・来る・帰る).
sections.formula: [Time] に + [Vehicle] で + [Place] で + [Object] を + [Verb]

examples.target: 毎日、バスで大学へ行って、図書館で勉強します。
examples.translation: Every day I go to university by bus and study at the library.

examples.target: 夜十時ごろ、うちへ帰りました。
examples.translation: I returned home around 10:00 p.m.

sections.proTip: Adding ごろ after a time means "around/approximately" (七時ごろ) and makes particle に optional.

vocabCards.example: 毎朝七時に起きます。
vocabCards.exampleNote: Ichidan verb (dictionary form: 起きる).

vocabCards.example: 昼ごはんにラーメンを食べました。
vocabCards.exampleNote: Takes direct object particle を.

vocabCards.example: 週末、スーパーへ行きます。
vocabCards.exampleNote: Destination takes へ or に.

vocabCards.pronunciation: べんきょうします (benkyō shimasu)
vocabCards.example: カフェで日本語を勉強します。
vocabCards.exampleNote: Compound する-verb; action place takes で.

vocabCards.example: 六時にうちへ帰りました。
vocabCards.exampleNote: Careful: Godan verb (帰る → 帰って), not Ichidan!

practiceQuestions.prompt: Fill in the two particles: 「昨日、友だち___レストラン___昼ごはんを食べました。」
practiceQuestions.explanation: と marks companion ("with a friend") and で marks the action location ("at a restaurant").

practiceQuestions.prompt: Listen to Kenji’s schedule. How does he go to work?
practiceQuestions.audioScript: 私は毎朝六時半に起きます。朝ごはんを食べて、七時半に電車で会社へ行きます。夜は家で日本語の本を読みます。
practiceQuestions.explanation: He says 「電車で会社へ行きます」 (goes to the company by train).

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which time expression does NOT take particle に?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Relative time words like 昨日, 今日, 明日, 毎日 never take に.

lesson.checkpointModelAnswer: 私は毎朝七時に起きます。家で朝ごはんを食べて、八時に電車で会社へ行きます。昨日は仕事の後で友だちと渋谷のレストランで晩ごはんを食べました。十時にうちへ帰って、少し日本語を勉強しました。

modules.title: い-Adjectives vs. な-Adjectives, Preferences & Polite Invitations
modules.summary: Describe food, cities, and weather using both Japanese adjective families, express likes/skills with が, and invite friends warmly with 〜ませんか and 〜ましょう.
objectives: Conjugate い-adjectives (高い → 高くない / 高かった) and な-adjectives (静か → 静かじゃない / 静かだった) accurately.
Express preferences and abilities with 「〜が好きです / 上手です / わかります」.
Make warm invitations (一緒に行きませんか) and accept enthusiastically (ええ、行きましょう!).
grammarCheckpoints: い-adjectives (〜くない / 〜かった) vs. な-adjectives (〜なN / 〜じゃありません)
Preference & skill particle が (好き・きらい・上手・下手)
Invitations: 〜ませんか (won’t you?) & 〜ましょう (let’s!)

drills.title: Weekend Café Invitation Roleplay
drills.instruction: Invite a friend to a new restaurant, describe the food and atmosphere, and agree on a meeting time.

drills.title: Kyoto Trip Impressions
drills.instruction: Listen and catch what the speaker thought about Kyoto’s temples and food.
drills.audioScript: 先週、京都へ行きました。お寺はとても静かできれいでした。抹茶のアイスもすごくおいしかったです。でも、駅は少しにぎやかでした。

modules.checkpointPrompt: Describe your favorite city or restaurant in Japanese using both い-adjectives and な-adjectives, and invite a friend to visit with you.

lesson.overview: Bring vivid color to your Japanese by mastering the two adjective conjugation systems and inviting others smoothly with 〜ませんか and 〜ましょう.

sections.heading: い-Adjectives vs. な-Adjectives: Don’t Mix Their Endings!
sections.explanation: い-adjectives inflect directly (おいしい → おいしくない / おいしかった). な-adjectives behave like nouns and attach な ONLY before a noun (静かな町, きれいな花). Watch the famous impostors: きれい (pretty/clean) and 有名 (famous) end in -i sound, yet are な-adjectives!
sections.formula: い-adj: drop い + くない (neg) / かった (past)  |  な-adj: + な + Noun / じゃありません / でした

examples.target: このラーメンはあまり辛くなかったですが、とてもおいしかったです。
examples.translation: This ramen was not very spicy, and it was very delicious.
examples.highlight: 辛くなかった / おいしかったです

examples.target: 京都はきれいで有名な町です。
examples.translation: Kyoto is a beautiful and famous town.

sections.proTip: Remember irregular いい (good): all its conjugations revert to the stem よ- → よくない (not good), よかった (was good), よくなかった (was not good)!

sections.heading: Warm Invitations: 〜ませんか vs. 〜ましょう
sections.explanation: Use 〜ませんか ("Won’t you ...?") to give the listener polite room to accept or decline. Once you are suggesting a shared next step or accepting an invitation, switch to enthusiastic 〜ましょう ("Let’s ...!").
sections.formula: Invitation: [Verb stem] + ませんか  |  Agreement/Suggestion: [Verb stem] + ましょう

examples.target: 土曜日、一緒に映画を見ませんか。— ええ、ぜひ見ましょう！
examples.translation: Won’t you watch a movie together on Saturday? — Yes, let’s definitely see one!
examples.highlight: 見ませんか / 見ましょう

examples.target: 私は音楽が好きです。今度コンサートへ行きませんか。
examples.translation: I like music. Won’t you go to a concert sometime soon?

sections.proTip: Pair あまり with a NEGATIVE predicate to soften criticism politely: 「あまり高くないです」(It’s not very expensive).

vocabCards.example: 日本のカレーはとてもおいしいです。
vocabCards.exampleNote: Past form: おいしかったです.

vocabCards.example: 図書館はいつも静かな場所です。
vocabCards.exampleNote: Needs な before a noun: 静かな部屋.

vocabCards.example: 昨日のパーティーは本当に楽しかったです。
vocabCards.exampleNote: Contrast with うれしい (happy/glad about an event).

vocabCards.example: どんな食べ物が好きですか。
vocabCards.exampleNote: Object of liking takes が, NOT を!

vocabCards.example: 今晩、一緒に晩ごはんを食べませんか。
vocabCards.exampleNote: Watch the small っ pause: i-s-sho (3 morae).

practiceQuestions.prompt: Select the correct past tense of 「いい天気です」(It is good weather):
options: いい天気でした / 天気がよかったです
practiceQuestions.explanation: いい conjugates from its よ- stem: 天気がよかったです (or noun + でした: いい天気でした).

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which adjective is a な-adjective (takes な before a noun) despite ending in い?
practiceQuestions.explanation: きれい (pretty/clean) is a な-adjective: きれいな公園 (NOT *きれいくない*).

practiceQuestions.prompt: Listen to the trip report. How did the speaker describe the station in Kyoto?
practiceQuestions.audioScript: 先週、京都へ行きました。お寺はとても静かできれいでした。抹茶のアイスもすごくおいしかったです。でも、駅は少しにぎやかでした。
practiceQuestions.explanation: She says 「駅は少しにぎやかでした」 (the station was a bit lively/bustling).

lesson.checkpointModelAnswer: 私の好きな町は京都です。古いお寺が多くて、とてもきれいな町です。食べ物もあまり高くなくて、本当においしいです。今度の週末、一緒に京都へ行きませんか。おいしい抹茶のケーキを食べましょう！

modules.title: Te-Form Requests, Ongoing Actions (〜ています) & JLPT N5 Simulation
modules.summary: Unlock the powerhouse Te-Form for polite requests (〜てください), permission (〜てもいいですか), prohibition (〜てはいけません), ongoing states (〜ています), and full N5 readiness.
objectives: Convert Ichidan, Godan, and Irregular verbs into accurate Te-Form without hesitation.
Make polite requests, ask permission, and understand public prohibition signs.
Pass the LinguaVerve Japanese A1 / JLPT N5 4-Skill Simulated Exam.
grammarCheckpoints: Te-Form requests (〜てください) & chaining actions (V1て、V2)
Permission (〜てもいいですか) & Prohibition (〜てはいけません)
Present progressive & resultant states (〜ています)

drills.title: Museum Rules & Guide Announcement
drills.instruction: Listen and identify what visitors are allowed to do and what is prohibited.
drills.audioScript: みなさん、美術館へようこそ。ロビーで水を飲んでもいいですが、展示室の中で写真を撮ってはいけません。荷物はロッカーに入れてください。

drills.title: N5 Email Comprehension Check
drills.instruction: Read Sakura’s message and note what she is currently doing and her request.
drills.samplePassage: ケンジさん、今、新宿駅の南口で待っています。電車が五分おくれましたから、急がなくてもいいですよ。着いたら電話をかけてください。

modules.checkpointPrompt: Write a short Japanese message to a visiting friend giving 2 polite requests and 1 museum/station rule using Te-Form patterns.

lesson.overview: Combine everything from A1/N5 using the Te-Form Swiss-army knife: requests, permissions, prohibitions, and ongoing actions.

sections.heading: Te-Form Survival Toolkit: Requests, Permission & Rules
sections.explanation: Once you know the Te-Form of a verb, four indispensable JLPT N5 patterns unlock instantly: 〜てください (please do), 〜てもいいですか (may I ...?), 〜てはいけません (must not ...), and V1て、V2 (do V1 and then V2).
sections.formula: Vて + ください (please)  |  Vて + もいいですか (may I?)  |  Vて + はいけません (must not)

examples.target: すみません、ここで写真を撮ってもいいですか。— いいえ、撮ってはいけません。
examples.translation: Excuse me, may I take photos here? — No, you must not take photos.
examples.highlight: 撮ってもいいですか / 撮ってはいけません

examples.target: もう少しゆっくり話してください。
examples.translation: Please speak a little more slowly.

sections.proTip: When someone asks 〜てもいいですか and you want to refuse gently in real life, soften 〜てはいけません to 「すみません、ちょっと…」 or 「ご遠慮ください」.

sections.heading: Two Meanings of 〜ています (Right Now vs. Ongoing State)
sections.explanation: With action verbs (食べる・待つ・勉強する), 〜ています means "is doing right now". With change-of-state verbs (住む・知る・結婚する・持つ), 〜ています means a continuing state ("lives in", "knows", "is married").
sections.formula: Action V + ています (in progress)  |  State-change V + ています (current state)

examples.target: 今、カフェで友だちを待っています。
examples.translation: Right now I am waiting for a friend at the café.

examples.target: 山田さんの電話番号を知っていますか。— いいえ、知りません。
examples.translation: Do you know Yamada’s phone number? — No, I do not know it.
examples.highlight: 知っています / 知りません

sections.proTip: Classic N5 trap: The negative of 知っています (I know) is 「知りません」, NEVER *"知っていません"*!

vocabCards.example: ちょっと待ってください。すぐ行きます。
vocabCards.exampleNote: 待つ (Godan -つ) → 待って.

vocabCards.example: 公園できれいな写真を撮りました。
vocabCards.exampleNote: Verb collocation: 写真を撮る (to take a photo).

vocabCards.example: どうぞここに座ってください。
vocabCards.exampleNote: Seat destination takes に (いすに座る).

vocabCards.example: このパソコンを使ってもいいですか。
vocabCards.exampleNote: 使う (Godan -う) → 使って.

vocabCards.example: 日本語が少しわかります。
vocabCards.exampleNote: Takes が for the understood item, not を.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Listen to the museum announcement. What is NOT allowed inside the exhibition room?
practiceQuestions.audioScript: みなさん、美術館へようこそ。ロビーで水を飲んでもいいですが、展示室の中で写真を撮ってはいけません。荷物はロッカーに入れてください。
options: Taking photos in the exhibition room
practiceQuestions.explanation: 展示室の中で写真を撮ってはいけません = you must not take photos inside the exhibition room.

practiceQuestions.prompt: How do you reply "No, I do not know" to 「田中さんの住所を知っていますか」?
options: いいえ、知っていません。
いいえ、知らなくてもいいです。
practiceQuestions.explanation: The negative of 知っています is always 知りません.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Choose the right Te-Form of 読む (to read) and 行く (to go):
practiceQuestions.explanation: 読む (-む → んで) becomes 読んで; irregular exception 行く becomes 行って.

lesson.checkpointModelAnswer: ミアさん、今、東京駅の北口で待っています。駅に着いたら、メッセージをください。それから、今日は美術館へ行きますね。美術館の中で写真を撮ってはいけませんが、ロビーでコーヒーを飲んでもいいですよ。あとで会いましょう！

intensiveCourses.title: Japanese A2 / JLPT N4 Everyday Independence Intensive
intensiveCourses.subtitle: Automate Plain Forms, quoting (〜と思います), potential & conditional verbs, giving/receiving (あげる・くれる・もらう), transitive/intransitive states, and everyday polite advice.
intensiveCourses.passingCriteria: JLPT N4 scaled score ≥ 90/180 (min 38/120 Language Knowledge & Reading, 19/60 Listening) + fluent everyday interaction.

modules.summary: Unlock the Plain Form (普通形) engine required for expressing opinions (〜と思います), reporting speech (〜と言いました), modifying nouns, and giving explanations (〜んです).
objectives: Convert any verb/adjective cleanly into Dictionary, ない, た, and なかった plain forms.
Embed plain clauses naturally before 〜と思います, 〜と言いました, and 〜んです.
Modify nouns directly with whole Japanese clauses (「昨日買ったカメラ」).
grammarCheckpoints: Plain Form 4-way grid (辞書形・ない形・た形・なかった)
Quoting with 〜と思います / 〜と言っていました

drills.title: Reported Schedule Change
drills.instruction: Listen and catch what Teacher Sato said about Friday’s class.
drills.audioScript: 佐藤先生は、金曜日のテストはやさしいから心配しなくてもいいと言っていましたよ。でも、辞書を忘れないでねと言いました。

drills.title: Opinion & Explanation Sprint
drills.instruction: Give 3 opinions about learning Japanese using 〜と思います and explain why with 〜んです.

modules.checkpointPrompt: Write a short Japanese paragraph sharing your opinion about living in a big city vs. a small town using 〜と思います and two noun-modifying clauses.

lesson.overview: Cross the N5→N4 threshold by mastering Plain Forms — the indispensable building block inside almost every complex Japanese sentence.

sections.heading: Plain Form Before 〜と思います & 〜と言いました
sections.explanation: Even when speaking politely to a boss or teacher, everything BEFORE と (quoting particle) switches to Plain Form. Remember that な-adjectives and nouns keep だ before と: 「便利だと思います」(I think it’s convenient).
sections.formula: [Plain Form (V / い-adj / な-adjだ / Nだ)] + と思います / と言いました

examples.target: 明日はたぶん雨が降らないと思います。
examples.translation: I think it probably won’t rain tomorrow.

examples.target: 田中さんは、新しいレストランはとても静かだと言っていました。
examples.translation: Tanaka was saying that the new restaurant is very quiet.
examples.highlight: 静かだと言っていました

sections.proTip: Forming ない-form for Godan verbs: shift the final -u vowel to -a + ない (書く→書かない), EXCEPT verbs ending in bare う become わない (買う→買わない, NOT *かあない*) and ある becomes simply ない!

sections.heading: Japanese Relative Clauses (Modifier BEFORE Noun!)
sections.explanation: Japanese has no words like "who", "which", or "that". Simply place a Plain Form clause directly in front of the noun it describes! Note that inside a modifying clause, the subject takes が or の, NEVER は.
sections.formula: [Plain Form Clause (subject + が)] + [Noun]

examples.target: これは去年、京都で買ったお茶碗です。
examples.translation: This is the tea bowl that I bought in Kyoto last year.

examples.target: あそこで赤いコートを着ている人は山田さんです。
examples.translation: The person wearing a red coat over there is Yamada.
examples.highlight: 赤いコートを着ている人

sections.proTip: Never put polite ます/です inside a noun-modifying clause: say 「母が作った料理」(the dish my mother made), NEVER *"母が作りました料理"*.

vocabCards.example: この映画は面白いと思います。
vocabCards.exampleNote: Use 思っています for another person’s ongoing opinion.

vocabCards.example: 駅員さんは五分おくれると言いました。
vocabCards.exampleNote: Pronounced "yū" in natural dictionary form.

vocabCards.example: 先生の説明はとてもわかりやすかったです。
vocabCards.exampleNote: Verb form: 説明する (to explain).

vocabCards.example: 土曜日、友だちと食事の約束があります。
vocabCards.exampleNote: Collocation: 約束を守る (keep a promise).

vocabCards.example: 電車の中に傘を忘れてしまいました。
vocabCards.exampleNote: Ichidan verb → ない-form: 忘れない.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which sentence correctly says "I think Tokyo is convenient"?
options: 東京は便利ですと思います。
東京は便利だと思います。
東京は便利と思います。
practiceQuestions.explanation: な-adjectives (便利) require plain copula だ before と思います.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Choose the natural relative clause for "the book my friend lent me":
options: 友だちが貸してくれた本
友だちは貸しました本
practiceQuestions.explanation: Inside a relative clause, use Plain Form + が (not は or ます), placed before the noun 本.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Listen carefully. What did Teacher Sato remind students NOT to forget?
practiceQuestions.audioScript: 佐藤先生は、金曜日のテストはやさしいから心配しなくてもいいと言っていましたよ。でも、辞書を忘れないでねと言いました。
practiceQuestions.explanation: 「辞書を忘れないでね」 = please don’t forget your dictionary.

lesson.checkpointModelAnswer: 私は大きい町より小さい町のほうが住みやすいと思います。大きい町はお店が多くて便利ですが、毎日電車がとてもこむからです。去年、旅行で行った金沢はとても静かで食べ物が美味しい町でした。いつかそういう町に住みたいと思っています。

modules.title: Experiences (〜たことがある), Plans (〜つもり) & Multitasking (〜ながら)
modules.summary: Share life experiences, list representative activities (〜たり〜たりする), state concrete intentions (〜つもり), and describe simultaneous actions (〜ながら).
objectives: Talk about life experiences accurately with Vた + ことがある (not Vる + ことがある).
Describe weekend routines naturally with Vたり Vたりします.
State personal plans and simultaneous habits using 〜つもりです and 〜ながら.
grammarCheckpoints: Past experience Vたことがある vs. occasional habit Vることがある
Representative actions: V1たり V2たりします
Intentions (Vる/Vない + つもり) & Simultaneous actions (Vます-stem + ながら)

drills.title: Hokkaido Travel Blog Scan
drills.instruction: Read the short blog and list what the author plans to do in Sapporo.
drills.samplePassage: 私はまだ北海道へ行ったことがありませんが、来月初めて行くつもりです。札幌でラーメンを食べたり、きれいな公園を散歩したりしたいです。

drills.title: 60-Second Bucket List & Weekend Routine
drills.instruction: Share 1 thing you have done, 1 thing you have never done, and 2 things you do on weekends using 〜たり〜たり.

modules.checkpointPrompt: Describe a travel experience you have had and your plans for your next holiday using 〜たことがある, 〜たり〜たり, and 〜つもりです.

lesson.overview: Move past basic schedules into rich personal storytelling — contrasting past life experiences, concrete future intentions, and simultaneous actions.

sections.heading: Life Experiences (〜たことがある) & Representative Lists (〜たり〜たり)
sections.explanation: Attach ことがある to the plain past た-form to mean "have had the experience of doing". To list sample activities without claiming the list is exhaustive, attach り to the た-form and close with する!
sections.formula: Vた + ことがあります (have done)  |  V1たり、V2たり します (do things like V1 and V2)

examples.target: 富士山に登ったことがありますか。— いいえ、一度もありません。
examples.translation: Have you ever climbed Mt. Fuji? — No, not even once.
examples.highlight: 登ったことがありますか

examples.target: 日曜日は掃除をしたり、音楽を聞いたりします。
examples.translation: On Sundays I do things like cleaning and listening to music.
examples.highlight: 掃除をしたり、音楽を聞いたりします

sections.proTip: Watch the tense trap: Vる + ことがある means "sometimes happens" (電車がおくれることがある), whereas Vた + ことがある means "have experienced before"!

sections.heading: Intentions (〜つもり) & Simultaneous Actions (〜ながら)
sections.explanation: Use Vる/Vない + つもりです for firm personal plans ("I intend to / not to"). Use V1(ます-stem) + ながら + V2 when ONE person does two actions at the same time — the MAIN action always sits at the end (V2)!
sections.formula: Vる / Vない + つもりです  |  [Background V1 stem] + ながら + [Main V2]

examples.target: 来年、日本の大学院へ留学するつもりです。
examples.translation: Next year I intend to study abroad at a Japanese graduate school.

examples.target: 毎朝、ポッドキャストを聞きながら駅まで歩きます。
examples.translation: Every morning I walk to the station while listening to a podcast.
examples.highlight: 聞きながら ... 歩きます

sections.proTip: Never omit します at the end of 〜たり〜たり: *"映画を見たり、買い物したりです"* is unnatural — always finish with します / しました!

vocabCards.example: 日本で働いた経験があります。
vocabCards.exampleNote: Also a する-verb: 経験する (to experience).

vocabCards.meaning: schedule / plan (more objective than つもり)
vocabCards.example: 来週、大阪へ出張する予定です。
vocabCards.exampleNote: Great for fixed itineraries and work plans.

vocabCards.example: 夏休みに九州へ旅行するつもりです。
vocabCards.exampleNote: Long final vowel: ryo-ko-u.

vocabCards.example: 家族のためにおみやげを選びました。
vocabCards.exampleNote: Godan -ぶ → 選んで / 選んだ.

vocabCards.example: 旅行の準備はもう終わりましたか。
vocabCards.exampleNote: Verb form: 準備する (to prepare).

practiceQuestions.prompt: What is the difference between 「納豆を食べたことがある」 and 「納豆を食べることがある」?
options: First = have tried eating natto before; Second = sometimes eat natto
Both mean "want to eat natto tomorrow"
First = never ate natto; Second = eat natto every day
practiceQuestions.explanation: Vたことがある = past life experience; Vることがある = occasional occurrence ("sometimes").

practiceQuestions.prompt: Choose the natural sentence for "I study while drinking tea":
options: お茶を飲んでながら勉強します。
お茶を飲みながら勉強します。
お茶を飲むながら勉強します。
practiceQuestions.explanation: ながら attaches directly to the ます-stem (飲み + ながら), not the て-form or dictionary form.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Listen to Haruka’s plan. Why is she saving money?
practiceQuestions.audioScript: 今年の冬はアルバイトをしながらお金をためて、春休みに沖縄へ行くつもりです。まだ沖縄へ行ったことがないんです。
options: To visit Okinawa during spring break for the first time
To move to Tokyo next month
practiceQuestions.explanation: She says 「春休みに沖縄へ行くつもりです。まだ沖縄へ行ったことがないんです。」

lesson.checkpointModelAnswer: 私は去年、初めて京都と奈良へ旅行したことがあります。古いお寺を見たり、おいしい和食を食べたりして、本当に楽しかったです。今年の秋は、日本語のポッドキャストを聞きながら旅行の準備をして、今度は北海道へ行くつもりです。

modules.title: Potential Form (られる・える) & Conditionals (〜と・〜たら・〜なら)
modules.summary: Express abilities and possibilities smoothly using Potential Verbs (話せる・食べられる・できる), and choose accurately among Japanese conditionals (と, たら, ば, なら).
objectives: Conjugate Ichidan, Godan, and Irregular verbs into Potential Form and pair them with particle が.
Select the right conditional: と (automatic/natural result), たら (general "if/when"), and なら (contextual advice).
Handle everyday travel and machine-operation instructions accurately.
grammarCheckpoints: Potential Form: Godan -u→-eru / Ichidan -る→-られる / する→できる / 来る→来られる
Conditional と (inevitable result / directions) vs. たら (versatile if/when)
Contextual conditional なら ("if it’s X, then I recommend...")

drills.title: Ticket Machine & Station Directions
drills.instruction: Listen and catch the exact conditional sequence to buy a ticket and reach the museum.
drills.audioScript: この青いボタンを押すと、英語の画面が出ますよ。切符を買ったら、東口から出て右へ曲がってください。まっすぐ歩くと美術館が見えます。
